world_behind.title: The wilderness child takes the stand
world_behind.text: The boy blessed in 2 Nephi 2 is now the colony's preacher, and his credentials open the sermon: "called of God, and ordained after the manner of his holy order" (v. 2), consecrated by Nephi (2 Ne. 5:26). The record's ministry has its first second-generation voice, and he begins exactly where his father's blessing aimed him.

cites.quote: called of God, and ordained after the manner of his holy order

spans.text: called of God, and ordained after the manner of his holy order

world_behind.title: A king in fact, if not in name
world_behind.text: The people look to Nephi "as a king or a protector" (v. 2): the crown he declined (2 Ne. 5:18) sits on him anyway in the people's regard. The record keeps both truths without smoothing them; office in this colony is function first, title never.

cites.quote: as a king or a protector

spans.text: as a king or a protector

world_behind.title: An assigned text
world_behind.text: "They are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak" (v. 4): Nephi assigns Isaiah, Jacob expounds it. The passage is the very one Nephi read to the family a generation earlier (1 Ne. 21), now preached to their children: Isaiah as the colony's standing curriculum, taught by its second teacher.

cites.quote: They are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak

spans.text: They are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak

world_behind.title: News by vision
world_behind.text: "The Lord has shown me that those who were at Jerusalem, from whence we came, have been slain and carried away captive" (v. 8): an ocean away from any messenger, the colony learns Jerusalem's fall by revelation. Confirmation of Lehi's oldest prophecy arrives through the same channel that gave it.

cites.quote: The Lord has shown me that those who were at Jerusalem, from whence we came, have been slain and carried away captive

spans.text: The Lord has shown me that those who were at Jerusalem, from whence we came, have been slain and carried away captive

world_behind.title: The second-time recovery
world_behind.text: "The Messiah will set himself again the second time to recover them" (v. 14) speaks Isaiah's own idiom: the Lord setting his hand "again the second time" to recover the remnant (Isa. 11:11). Jacob reads the two gatherings, from Babylon and from everywhere, as distinct acts of one program.

cites.quote: The Messiah will set himself again the second time to recover them

spans.text: The Messiah will set himself again the second time to recover them

world_behind.title: A congregation, assembled
world_behind.text: This is the record's first scene of formal public worship in the new world: a consecrated preacher, an assembled people, an announced text, and a sermon spanning days (2 Ne. 10:3's "in the last night the angel spake unto me" shows it resuming after a night). The colony of chapter 5's civilization list now has its worship life visible.

words.text: "Mine anxiety is great for you; and ye yourselves know that it ever has been" (v. 3): Lehi's word (2 Ne. 1:16), inherited by the son he blessed, worn as a chronic condition. The record's preachers introduce hard sermons this way on purpose: the audience is told first what the speaker carries for them, then what they must hear.

cites.quote: Mine anxiety is great for you; and ye yourselves know that it ever has been

spans.text: Mine anxiety is great for you; and ye yourselves know that it ever has been

words.text: "Set up my standard to the people" (v. 6): not a rule to be measured against, but a pole with a banner on it, planted where scattered people can see it and come to it. Moroni uses the word in that plain sense when he plants the standard of liberty on the towers (Alma 46:36). Nephi, reading this same line to his brothers, took the raised banner to be the Gentiles themselves (1 Ne. 22:6). Jacob leaves the image unexplained and spends his exposition on who does the gathering instead.

cites.quote: Set up my standard to the people

spans.text: Set up my standard to the people

words.text: The verb is the old permissive one. To suffer a thing is to allow it, the sense the record keeps for captives let go free (Alma 44:20) and for a king allowed to spend his days in service (Mosiah 2:12). Read that way, the clause divides two things a modern ear hears as one: many "shall be afflicted in the flesh" (v. 11), and that is permitted; the perishing is not. Preservation in this sermon is a limit set on harm.

cites.quote: shall be afflicted in the flesh

spans.text: shall be afflicted in the flesh

words.text: "The people of the Lord are they who wait for him; for they still wait for the coming of the Messiah" (v. 13): a people defined by posture. Waiting in Isaiah's clause carries its own promise, they "shall not be ashamed" (v. 7), and Jacob makes it the covenant's membership test: sustained expectation.

cites.quote: The people of the Lord are they who wait for him; for they still wait for the coming of the Messiah

spans.text: The people of the Lord are they who wait for him; for they still wait for the coming of the Messiah

words.text: The plural is the record's own. The word appears four times here and never in the King James Bible, which keeps it singular. Jacob lists it among six ways the unbelieving are destroyed: fire, tempest, earthquakes, bloodsheds, pestilence, famine. Lehi had used the same plural of what passes from one generation to the next (2 Ne. 1:12), so the form arrives already meaning a series of killings.

"The prey of the terrible shall be delivered" (v. 17): terrible names a person here, not a feeling. It is the older sense, the one who causes terror, and it stands beside "the captives of the mighty" so that the captor is described twice by what he does to other people: he is strong, and he frightens. The question of verse 16 assumed such a man could not be robbed. The answer takes his prisoners anyway.

cites.quote: The prey of the terrible shall be delivered

spans.text: The prey of the terrible shall be delivered

phrases.text: The people's own title for the brother who refused a crown. The record lets the phrase carry the colony's political reality: authority in the city of Nephi is a person trusted for "safety" (v. 2), not an institution, and the books ahead will wrestle with what happens when such persons die.

Lehi signed his farewell with one object, the everlasting welfare of his sons' souls (2 Ne. 2:30); Jacob opens his first recorded sermon with the same phrase as motive. The record's preaching dynasty passes down office and text, and with them the reason for speaking at all.

The sermon's interpretive license, granted before the reading begins. Likening here is entitlement: because the hearers are "of the house of Israel" (v. 5), Isaiah's words about Israel are legally theirs. The record's whole use of Isaiah, from Nephi's readings to the Savior's own commentary (3 Ne. 23), runs on this warrant.

phrases.term: Manifest himself unto them in the flesh
phrases.text: The sermon's center of gravity: the Holy One of Israel appearing as a mortal among the very people whose fall Jacob has just reported. Stated between a captivity and a crucifixion, the clause holds the record's terrible irony: the manifestation is to the covenant people, and by them he is "scourge" (v. 9)d and crucified.

phrases.term: The second time to recover them
phrases.text: Isaiah's second-gathering idiom, deployed as structure: one recovery from Babylon already shown (v. 9), one from everywhere still ahead. Jacob's reading gives the record its two-act map of Israel's future, and the test that sorts the acts' outcomes is single: "when that day cometh when they shall believe in him" (v. 14).

cites.quote: when that day cometh when they shall believe in him

spans.text: when that day cometh when they shall believe in him

phrases.term: None will he destroy that believe in him
phrases.text: The destruction catalogue of verse 15 (fire, tempest, earthquake, bloodshed, pestilence, famine) is fenced by this one exemption, stated first. Judgment in Jacob's preaching is never indiscriminate; belief is the whole boundary line, and the sentence's economy, none that believe, is its comfort.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: The credentials end in a brother
verses.text: Called of God, ordained after the manner of his holy order, "and having been consecrated by my brother Nephi, unto whom ye look as a king or a protector, and on whom ye depend for safety." Jacob's authority runs through family, and the title he attaches to Nephi is the people's, not Nephi's: 2 Nephi 5:18 has them wanting him for king and Nephi refusing. Jacob names the office his brother declined and does not correct the congregation.

verses.label: v. 4–5
verses.title: An assigned sermon, and the method stated twice
verses.text: "They are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak" (v. 4): the reading is a commission, not an impulse. Verse 5 then gives the rule for it and immediately repeats it, "they may be likened unto you, for ye are of the house of Israel," then "which may be likened unto you, because ye are of the house of Israel." The warrant is lineage, and Jacob states it twice in one verse before quoting a word.

cites.quote: They are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak

spans.text: They are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak

verses.label: v. 6–7
verses.title: He announces Isaiah and reads two verses
verses.text: The quotation runs from "Thus saith the Lord God" to "they shall not be ashamed that wait for me," which is Isaiah 49:22-23 and nothing more. Verse 8 breaks in with "And now I, Jacob, would speak somewhat concerning these words." Two verses of text carry eleven of exposition, and the chapter Jacob draws them from had already been copied out in full at 1 Nephi 21.

verses.label: v. 8–9
verses.title: The colony's news comes by angel
verses.text: "The Lord has shown me that those who were at Jerusalem, from whence we came, have been slain and carried away captive." A community with no correspondence learns the fate of its home city by revelation. Verse 9 does the same for an event still centuries off, the scourging and crucifixion, "according to the words of the angel who spake it unto me." Two verses, two facts, one source, and no other offered.

verses.label: v. 13
verses.title: The quoted image comes back pointed the other way
verses.text: In verse 7 the kings and queens of the Gentiles "lick up the dust of thy feet" as they bow to Israel. In verse 13 Jacob keeps the phrase and moves it: "they that fight against Zion and the covenant people of the Lord shall lick up the dust of their feet." The words appear three times in the volume, twice in this chapter, and the exposition turns the gesture from homage into defeat.

verses.label: v. 16–17
verses.title: The chapter's only question is a quotation
verses.text: "Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered?" is the single question mark in eighteen verses, and it is not Jacob's: Isaiah 49:24. He answers it the same way, by resuming the quotation he had left eight verses earlier, so the argument closes in the voice it opened in rather than in his own.

chapter.title: The curriculum institutionalized
chapter.text: Four institutional facts stand in three verses. The office: "having been called of God, and ordained after the manner of his holy order, and having been consecrated by my brother Nephi" at verse 2. The assignment: "they are the words which my brother has desired that I should speak unto you" at verse 4. The text: "the words which I shall read are they which Isaiah spake" at verse 5. The method: "they may be likened unto you, for ye are of the house of Israel," the same word used at 1 Nephi 19:23. Reading Isaiah aloud has become a commissioned duty performed by an ordained man on another man's instruction.eneration).

chapter.title: Motive precedes office
chapter.text: Jacob spends verse 2 on his credentials and verse 3 on his anxiety, and the order is a template: authority in the record's pulpits is licensed by love the audience can verify. Every great sermon ahead (Benjamin's, Alma's) opens with the same disclosure.

chapter.title: History hinges on recognition
chapter.text: In Jacob's outline the scattering runs on hardened hearts and the gathering on coming "to the knowledge of their Redeemer" (v. 11): the same cardiology Nephi taught (1 Ne. 22), now preached as settled doctrine. Israel's geography, in this record, is a function of what Israel knows about one person.

cites.quote: to the knowledge of their Redeemer

spans.text: to the knowledge of their Redeemer

chapter.title: The Gentiles get a three-clause test
chapter.text: Repent; fight not against Zion; join not the great and abominable church. The vision-cycle's categories (1 Ne. 13–14) reappear as live conditions, and the record's evenhandedness holds: the same covenant that gathers Israel blesses any Gentile who keeps the three clauses.

chapter.title: A doctrine sized for a small colony
chapter.text: Every promise in the reading concerns nations, kings, and world-scale gatherings; the hearers are one settlement an ocean from all of it. What the sermon gives them is a part they can actually play now, and Isaiah's not-ashamed clause guarantees the role is not a consolation prize.

chapter.title: Judgment is exact, never general
chapter.text: None that believe are destroyed; the catalogue falls on the rest. Jacob inherits his father's precision (the fire that refines one man and consumes another) and states it as the second coming's rule: the day sorts by belief.

chapter.title: A sermon built like a school lesson
chapter.text: Text (v. 6–7), exposition (v. 8–15), objection and answer (v. 16–18): the classical form, with the reading resumed at length in chapters 7–8, the doctrine argued in 9, and the application delivered in 10. The unit's architecture is visible from its first chapter.

applications.title: State your anxiety before your counsel
applications.text: Before the next hard conversation you must initiate, tell the person what you carry for them, in words they can verify from your history together. Correction offered from disclosed love lands as covenant.

applications.title: Take the assigned text
applications.text: Jacob preached what Nephi asked him to. When a teacher, leader, or parent hands you material that is not your choice, work it the way Jacob worked Isaiah: find the likening, and give it your own voice rather than your own agenda.

applications.title: Claim your mail
applications.text: Make Jacob's warrant personal: you are of the house the promises address. Take one scattering-and- gathering passage this week and read it as legally yours, because the license in this verse extends to every grafted branch.

applications.title: Run the Gentile test
applications.text: Its conditions are portable: repent; fight not against Zion; unite not with what merchandises souls. Run your commitments, memberships, and money through those conditions and see what passes.

applications.title: Join the waiters
applications.text: Write down what you are still actively expecting from God, promises unfulfilled that you have not quietly written off. If the list is empty, the verse's definition has located the problem; pick one promise and resume waiting for it on purpose.

applications.title: Let the prayers hold someone
applications.text: Israel was preserved through centuries of scattering because of the prayers of the faithful. Assign yourself one scattered person, far from covenant ground, and become part of the preserving: prayers in this verse have multi-generation reach.

questions.text: What office or role do I hold whose credential I state more readily than its motive?
Who in my life knows, from evidence, that my anxiety for them ever has been?
Which scripture promises do I still read as other people's, despite the likening warrant?
Whose eventual gathering might depend in part on prayers I have stopped praying?
What am I waiting for God to do, and would an observer call my posture waiting or merely elapsed time?
Does my confidence about the day of power rest on category, my people, my membership, or on the verse's actual boundary, belief in him?
